newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Lower avails support light grades.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Lower avails support light grades.

text.p: Trading on Asia's crude market remained thin, although a fall in Australian crude output in August should provide some support to the light sweet market, traders said on Wednesday.
Lower Cossack production could cut August availabilities to three cargoes, instead of the usual four, traders said.
In addition, the number of Kutubu cargoes in August is also expected to fall to three, due to a decline of the field.
Normally, four Kutubu cargoes are available each month.
Asia's light crude prices have been under pressure since June, as refinery maintenance shutdowns have reduced demand.
Malaysia's official crude prices will only be announced after July 8, officials said.
The Middle East crude market saw a surge in activity, as August cargoes of Abu Dhabi and Qatar crudes were traded.
An Oman cargo was sold by a U.S. refiner to its affiliated company, although the seller would not comment on price.
Various rumours were heard on the level of the deal, ranging from MPM -30 to MPM -40 cents per barrel, although most traders were certain the premium was closer to MPM -30.
Traders expect Abu Dhabi crude prices to remain steady around ADNOC -40 for August, but said Oman prices could fall further, as the fall in Oman MPM was not as deep as expected.
The official June Oman price was cut by $1.50 to $17.75.
At market close, Bangchak was heard still talking with a European major for the purchase of 800,000 barrels of Murban crude for its August tender.
The level was said agreed around Dubai +76, but the credit terms were still being negotiated, traders said.
Bangchak was heard asking for a one-year credit term from the supplier, although this was denied by Bangchak officials.
